entries.title: Warm editorial landing — paper, serif, and a reading rhythm
entries.summary: Original self-contained editorial homepage starter with an asymmetrical lead, CSS artwork, numbered article rows, and honest sample copy. A warm alternative to a generic card-grid hero.
entries.guidance: Use for a journal, independent publication, or text-led landing page where reading matters more than conversion widgets. Tokens: warm paper #f4efe4, ink #282b25, muted #575a50, terracotta #85391f; Georgia display headings plus system body text. Keep the fluid 1–3rem page space, thin rules, 13–15ch hero measure, and the three-part article-row rhythm together. The abstract CSS art is original and decorative context, not a stock photo. Adapt by replacing issue copy and article descriptions with owned writing, then linking real article destinations; translate semantic HTML to JSX without replacing headings or anchors with clickable divs. At 48rem the hero stacks and descriptions sit below titles. Check 320px widths, 200–400% zoom, long translated titles, keyboard skip link and visible focus, and contrast after retheming. No motion is authored; preserve the reduced-motion override if adding transitions. Tradeoff: the generous lead and serif hierarchy suit a small reading list, not a dense feed or a complex navigation system. This is a static UI starter, not a publishing backend, subscriber system, or evidence of an actual magazine.

entries.title: Restrained SaaS landing — one promise, a legible queue, and a workflow
entries.summary: Original product-page starter in cool ink and white: one purposeful CTA, a labeled static interface preview, ruled workflow columns, and native disclosure questions. No fake social proof or invented business outcomes.
entries.guidance: Use for an early product explanation when you can describe the job but do not yet have verified customer evidence. Tokens: #fbfcfc canvas, #172d39 ink, #4c626e secondary text, #15566e action, #b4c5cd rules; system typography, compact radii, 1.5–3rem section gaps. Keep one main action and show task language in the preview rather than a wall of feature cards. Adapt by replacing the fictional queue with truthful capabilities, wiring the CTA to a real destination, and adding proof only with consent and substantiation. Keep the preview labeled as an illustration unless it becomes interactive. Preserve native details/summary keyboard behavior and semantic ordered steps in React. At 48rem both hero and workflow become one column; status labels wrap below their tasks. Check 320px, large text, translated queue labels, contrast, visible focus and skip navigation. No authored motion; honor prefers-reduced-motion if introducing any. Tradeoff: this intentionally omits pricing, signup, testimonials, and feature sprawl; add those only when content and backend exist. Not an authenticated product, billing integration, or operational collaboration app.

entries.title: Dense analytics dashboard — dark ledger, aligned metrics, and readable tables
entries.summary: Original high-density read-only dashboard starter with a side index, four related counts, a zero-baseline CSS bar chart with a text equivalent, review notes, and a keyboard-scrollable data table. All numbers form a consistent fictional dataset.
entries.guidance: Use for operational analytics where comparisons and definitions matter more than ornamental charts. Tokens: #111c26 canvas, #182734 panels, #e6edf2 foreground, #b7c6d1 secondary text, #8dd6c7 values, #f2cb85 review emphasis; system text with tabular numerals, 1px ruled regions, 1.25rem panel padding. Counts reconcile: 240 received = 192 completed + 48 open; 12 needing review are part of open. Adapt by mapping real metrics, labeling window and timezone, handling unavailable or stale values, and maintaining the same semantics in React. The chart has a text equivalent and bars share a zero baseline; never imply color alone communicates status. At 64rem metrics become 2×2 and chart/notes stack; at 42rem navigation becomes a top row. The table keeps useful column width in an explicitly focusable scrolling region. Check keyboard horizontal scroll, screen-reader headers, 320px and 400% zoom, contrast, and accurate totals after any dataset change. No chart motion is authored; keep the reduced-motion rule if adding updates. Tradeoff: a table overflows intentionally rather than deleting columns; the layout is read-only and small-data, not ingestion, filtering, export, monitoring, or an authenticated analytics service.

entries.title: Portfolio case study — a typographic index of decisions and evidence
entries.summary: Original warm-white and plum portfolio composition with an oversized serif introduction, marginal metadata, an original CSS concept diagram, numbered design decisions, and an explicit unknowns section. No invented clients or success metrics.
entries.guidance: Use for explaining a small design project, a self-directed exercise, or a portfolio detail page. Tokens: #fffdf9 canvas, #252324 ink, #7b304c plum, #f1e9ec diagrams, #91868a separators; Georgia headings, system prose, monospace metadata; 1:2.2 marginal/content grid with 2rem gaps. The silhouette diagram uses only original CSS rectangles and labels. Adapt by replacing fictional brief, role, decisions, and unknowns with shareable work; distinguish observations from assumptions and add outcome numbers only with evidence. Use actual project links rather than placeholder contact buttons. Preserve dl metadata, article, ordered decision list, and a text equivalent for any new diagram. At 48rem margins move above content and metadata reflows to two columns. Test long job titles, 320px and 200–400% zoom, keyboard navigation and focus, and contrast when adjusting plum. No motion is authored; retain reduced-motion handling if adding a reveal. Tradeoff: the design prioritizes one deep study and leaves personal profiles, client logos, a multi-project gallery, CMS, and contact delivery unimplemented. This is an honest unvalidated composition starter, not a commissioned project or evidence of a client relationship.

entries.title: Commerce catalog — quiet object studies, local filters, and price order
entries.summary: Original sage catalog starter with three CSS object illustrations, clear sample prices, category and price controls, native product-note disclosures, and live result counts. Local filtering works without a fake cart or checkout.
entries.guidance: Use for a small product/category listing or a brand concept needing variation in object silhouette rather than endless identical cards. Tokens: #f8f8f2 paper, #22382e ink, #4d6256 secondary text, #285b43 control, #e4ecdf object wash; Georgia page title and system descriptions, square controls, 2rem product gaps. Three original CSS studies supply visual rhythm with no external assets. Adapt by replacing studies with owned/licensed product images, accurate currency/material data and meaningful details. The minimal JS filters category and sorts numerical prices; preserve stable IDs, native selects and role=status when moving to React state. All items remain readable without JS. Listing changes do not steal focus. At 58rem three columns become two and at 36rem become one; controls wrap with 44px minimum height. Check keyboard controls, result announcements, zoom, translations, contrast and the zero-results state when adding categories. No motion is authored; maintain the reduced-motion override if adding reorder animation. Tradeoff: the small in-memory dataset demonstrates filtering, not server pagination or real stock. Prices are explicitly fictional; cart, checkout, payments, tax, shipping and purchase promises are absent.

entries.title: Accessible settings flow — calm form, recoverable validation, and local feedback
entries.summary: Original slate-and-white preferences form starter with native labels, grouped choices, generous targets, an error summary that receives focus, linked field errors, and polite save/reset feedback. Only fictional local preferences are handled.
entries.guidance: Use for a small preferences or setup form where users need context and an obvious recovery path. Tokens: #f2f5f8 page, white form, #203344 ink, #485d6e help, #215278 action, #a0202b error; system typography, 1–2rem form inset, 1rem field gaps, 44px minimum controls. Keep the explanatory left column and two semantic fieldsets; comfortable density must not mean small controls. Adapt by replacing fictional display options with actual settings, adding server-side validation, authorization, persistence and network-failure recovery. The JS validates trimmed length, marks aria-invalid, reveals linked helper/error copy, focuses the error summary and reports outcomes through role=status using textContent, not HTML injection. In React preserve label IDs and focus the summary with a ref after rendering. Saved values are demo state only; no account, email or private data is requested. At 48rem context stacks above the form and action buttons wrap. Check empty/whitespace labels, keyboard summary link, checkbox descriptions, reset, 320px/400% zoom, translated copy and contrast. No authored motion; retain prefers-reduced-motion handling. Tradeoff: this is a short single-page flow, not a multi-step account wizard, secure authentication, notifications service or backend application.

entries.title: Flutter adaptive dashboard — hinge-aware notebook panes without tiny cards
entries.summary: Original complete Flutter Material starter app using local queue selection, semantic headings and scrollable regions. LayoutBuilder adapts compact/wide screens while MediaQuery display features partition around a vertical or horizontal hinge/fold.
entries.guidance: Use for a local operations or reading dashboard that needs compact, wide and folding-device layouts without fixed text heights. Complete main.dart source imports only Flutter Material and dart:ui. Tokens: #f5f4ee warm surface, #1e3037 ink, #244f61 action, #e2e9eb selection, #738891 rules; Material 3 system text, 24px pane space, 48px queue targets, flat ruled content rather than decorative tiles. Adapt by pasting source into an existing current-stable Flutter project's lib/main.dart, replacing fictional queues with a defined model and connecting persistence separately. LayoutBuilder stacks under 800 logical pixels; wide layouts have separately scrollable queue/detail panes. Display-feature screen coordinates are offset for SafeArea, and a single separating vertical or horizontal hinge/fold creates two usable regions; when a region is too small the larger side carries the whole flow. Preserve ReadingOrderTraversalPolicy, selected semantics, live queue heading and text counts. Check emulator hinge bounds, portrait/landscape, a zero-width fold, safe insets, 320px width, 200% text scale, keyboard Tab/Enter/Space and TalkBack/VoiceOver; validate contrast after theming. No custom animation is authored and theme animation is zero; for added transitions derive durations from MediaQuery.disableAnimations and respect accessibleNavigation. Tradeoff: only the first separating feature is partitioned; multiple hinges, platform window management and backend analytics are out of scope. This is a complete UI starter app with in-memory data, not a production service.

entries.title: Flutter accessible onboarding — quiet choices, intentional empty state, and reset
entries.summary: Original complete Flutter starter app with a two-step introduction, an optional off-by-default reminder preference, skip/back controls, a helpful empty reading list, and a local sample-item loop. Text reflows and focus follows step headings.
entries.guidance: Use for a calm first-run experience or an empty-state flow that gives one understandable next action instead of requesting accounts or permission prematurely. Tokens: #fcf6ef warm surface, #30262e ink, #6a3655 plum action, #665360 secondary text, #8a7582 rules; Material system body, serif-designated heading, 20–32px page padding, 600px reading measure and 48px buttons. Original page-shape art uses Containers only. Adapt by placing complete source in lib/main.dart of an existing current-stable Flutter project, replacing the sample prompt with an owned data model, then implementing storage or permissions explicitly. The optional reminder is off by default and clearly sends nothing; no personal data is requested. Skip, Back, local add/remove and Restart work. A disposable FocusNode moves keyboard focus to the new semantic live heading after step rendering; reading-order traversal and native CheckboxListTile retain keyboard/assistive semantics. SingleChildScrollView, ConstrainedBox and Wrap avoid fixed-height text and button overflow. Test 320px, tablet and landscape widths, 200% text scale, keyboard traversal, step focus, checkbox toggle, TalkBack/VoiceOver announcements and reset. No authored motion; theme changes have zero duration, and any added transition must honor MediaQuery.disableAnimations/accessibility settings. Tradeoff: a deliberately short local flow, not authentication, notification scheduling, an external article feed or durable preference storage. The empty state is not an error and never invents business claims.
